residency.test: Resident after 183 days in any 12-month period, or if you have a permanent place of abode in New Zealand regardless of days.
residency.permanent_place_of_abode: This overrides the day count and is judged on the whole picture - property, family, social and economic ties. It is why some people remain New Zealand tax resident years after leaving.
residency.transitional_resident: New migrants and returning New Zealanders after ten years abroad get a four-year exemption on most foreign income.

headline.no_capital_gains_tax: no general CGT, though the bright-line test taxes some property sales
headline.kiwisaver: 3% employee and 3% employer as the default

income_tax.name: Income tax (PAYE)
income_tax.note: full-year rates for the year ending 31 March 2026

employee.name: KiwiSaver employee contribution
employee.note: default rate; 4%, 6%, 8% and 10% may be chosen. Opt-out is possible within 8 weeks of starting a job

employer.name: KiwiSaver employer contribution
employer.note: subject to employer superannuation contribution tax

capital_gains.general: New Zealand has no comprehensive capital gains tax
capital_gains.bright_line_test: residential property sold within two years of acquisition is taxed as income, with a main home exclusion. The period was reduced from ten years to two from 1 July 2024
capital_gains.intention_test: gains are taxable if the asset was acquired with the purpose of resale - this catches traders regardless of the bright-line period
capital_gains.fif_rules: foreign shares costing over 50,000 NZD are taxed annually on a deemed 5% return under the foreign investment fund rules, whether or not you sell

quirks: The foreign investment fund rules are the biggest surprise for migrants. Holding more than 50,000 NZD of foreign shares means paying tax each year on a deemed return, even with no dividends and no sale.
There is no joint filing and no spousal transfer. Each person is taxed entirely separately.
The tax year ends 31 March. Most employees have nothing to do - Inland Revenue issues an automatic income tax assessment in May or June.
KiwiSaver employer contributions are taxed (ESCT) at your marginal rate, so the headline 3% match is worth less than it appears.
Working for Families tax credits are income-tested on family income and are squared up after year end, which frequently produces a debt for families whose income rose during the year.

reporting.who_must_file: Salary and wage earners usually receive an automatic income tax assessment and file nothing. An IR3 return is required for business income, rental income, foreign income, or income without PAYE deducted.

deadlines.what: IR3 return for the year ended 31 March 2026
Extended deadline if linked to a tax agent

Provisional tax instalments under the standard option

forms.name: Adjust your income for Working for Families and student loans

documents_to_collect: Summary of earnings, which IRD holds already from employer payday filing
Bank and investment income statements including resident withholding tax deducted
Foreign share holdings and their cost, for the FIF calculation
Rental property income and expenses, including interest limitation details
Donation receipts - a 33.33% credit is available on charitable giving

penalties.late_payment: 1% immediately, a further 4% after seven days, then use-of-money interest
penalties.shortfall: 20% for lack of reasonable care, up to 150% for evasion

warnings: KiwiSaver is a savings contribution, not a tax. It reduces take-home pay but the money remains yours - treat it separately when comparing countries.
The independent earner tax credit and Working for Families credits are not modelled.
Student loan repayments of 12% above the annual threshold are not included.
